chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from his father, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a woman who was menstruating in Ramadan, then when the day had advanced she saw purity, he said: “She breaks her fast for that entire day, eating and drinking, then she makes it up.”
And concerning a woman who began the morning in Ramadan in a state of purity, then when the day had advanced she saw menstruation, he said: “She breaks her fast for that entire day.”

key_terms.تَقْضِيهِ: she makes it up later as a compensatory fast
key_terms.تُفْطِرُ: she breaks the fast; she does not continue fasting that day
key_terms.حَاضَتْ: she menstruated; entered the state of hayd
key_terms.طَاهِرًا: in a state of ritual purity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's fast in Ramadan if her menstruation ends or begins during the day?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding fasting in Ramadan for women whose state changes between menstruation and purity during the daytime. It states that if purity begins or menstruation starts after the day has advanced, the fast of that day is not observed as valid, and in the first case the day must be made up later.
